pc-develop-lib.meta.description: Reusable registration and data-generation modules for Minecraft development.
pc-develop-lib.lead: Reusable registration and data-generation modules for Minecraft development.
pc-develop-lib.overview: PC Develop Lib V2 is a foundation for Minecraft Fabric development. It organizes content registration and language and tag data generation into modules that can be reused across mod projects.
pc-develop-lib.features.1.title: Content registration
pc-develop-lib.features.1.description: Modules for registering items, blocks, item groups, points of interest and villagers.
pc-develop-lib.features.2.title: Language data generation
pc-develop-lib.features.2.description: The data-generation entry point demonstrates Chinese and English language factories.
pc-develop-lib.features.3.title: Tag data generation
pc-develop-lib.features.3.description: Example configurations cover item tags and point-of-interest type tags.
pc-develop-lib.steps.1.title: Review the project setup
pc-develop-lib.steps.1.description: The current source configuration uses Java 25, Minecraft 1.21.10 and Fabric. Review the repository’s build configuration first.
pc-develop-lib.steps.2.title: Explore registration examples
pc-develop-lib.steps.2.description: Start with the register module and the accompanying test examples to see how the registration modules fit together.
pc-develop-lib.steps.3.title: Explore data generation
pc-develop-lib.steps.3.description: Read the language and tag configuration in PCDevelopLibDataGenerator.java, then explore the accompanying examples.

piscescup-easy.meta.description: Straightforward whitelist, operator and ban management by player name.
piscescup-easy.lead: Straightforward whitelist, operator and ban management by player name.
piscescup-easy.overview: PiscesCup Easy is a Fabric mod that simplifies Minecraft player management. It brings whitelists, operators, bans and language settings together under one command. The README recommends server-side use.
piscescup-easy.features.1.title: Whitelist management
piscescup-easy.features.1.description: Add or remove whitelist entries by player name to manage server access.
piscescup-easy.features.2.title: Operators and bans
piscescup-easy.features.2.description: Manage operators and player-name bans through a consistent set of commands.
piscescup-easy.features.3.title: Language settings
piscescup-easy.features.3.description: Read the current language and switch command feedback between Chinese and English.
piscescup-easy.steps.1.title: Read the usage guide
piscescup-easy.steps.1.description: Review the README and command documentation, and check that the build matches your Minecraft version.
piscescup-easy.steps.2.title: Manage the whitelist
piscescup-easy.steps.2.description: With the required administrative permissions, use the command below and replace TestPlayer with the actual player name.
piscescup-easy.steps.3.title: Choose the message language
piscescup-easy.steps.3.description: Use the language-setting command to select zh_cn or en_us.
piscescup-easy.example.caption: Commands from the README
piscescup-easy.example.label: Player-management command example
piscescup-easy.example.code:
/pc_easy whitelist add TestPlayer
/pc_easy setting lang set en_us
more-advancements.meta.description: Fresh advancement challenges for familiar adventures and everyday activities.
more-advancements.lead: Fresh advancement challenges for familiar adventures and everyday activities.
more-advancements.overview: More Advancements adds extra Minecraft advancements and playful objectives. From exploring dimensions to everyday activities, it offers more challenges to try, with text available in Chinese and English.
more-advancements.features.1.title: Themed advancements
more-advancements.features.1.description: Generated advancement data is organized into adventure, End, husbandry, Minecraft and Nether categories.
more-advancements.features.2.title: Playful objectives
more-advancements.features.2.description: Existing objectives include collecting heads, observing mobs through a spyglass and eating a chorus fruit.
more-advancements.features.3.title: Chinese and English text
more-advancements.features.3.description: The repository includes zh_cn and en_us advancement titles and descriptions.
more-advancements.steps.1.title: Meet the project
more-advancements.steps.1.description: Read the README to learn about the project’s goal of adding advancement challenges.
more-advancements.steps.2.title: Explore the advancements
more-advancements.steps.2.description: Browse the generated advancement data alongside the language files to explore each objective’s title and description.
more-advancements.steps.3.title: Suggest an objective
more-advancements.steps.3.description: Have an idea for a new advancement? The README welcomes suggestions through GitHub Issues.
commons-lib.meta.description: Reusable everyday utilities to cut down on repetitive Java code.
commons-lib.lead: Reusable everyday utilities to cut down on repetitive Java code.
commons-lib.overview: Commons Lib is a general-purpose Java 21 library with validation helpers, common data structures and functional-programming utilities. Its reusable, loosely coupled components can be added to your project through Maven.
commons-lib.features.1.title: Utilities and validation
commons-lib.features.1.description: String, array and comparison helpers, plus null, argument and state validation.
commons-lib.features.2.title: Structured values
commons-lib.features.2.description: Intervals, Pair, fixed-arity tuples, and simple and atomic counters.
commons-lib.features.3.title: Extended functional interfaces
commons-lib.features.3.description: Multi-argument, primitive-specialized and throwable interfaces, with currying, partial application and memoization.
commons-lib.steps.1.title: Use Java 21
commons-lib.steps.1.description: Use Java 21 or a compatible newer environment for your project.
commons-lib.steps.2.title: Choose a build tool and copy
commons-lib.steps.2.description: Select a version and dependency format, then click Copy dependency. Paste the code into the corresponding build configuration.
commons-lib.steps.3.title: Start with the examples
commons-lib.steps.3.description: The README includes quick examples for naming conversions, intervals, counters, functions and Pair.

linq.title: LINQ for Java · PiscesCup
linq.description: LINQ for Java: an Enumerable query library for Java 25, featuring fluent queries, deferred execution and primitive-specialized sequences.
linq.lead: Turn data processing into composable queries with a familiar LINQ style.
linq.overview: LINQ for Java brings an Enumerable query model to Java collections and sequences. Compose processing steps with where, select and orderBy; many intermediate operations execute when the results are enumerated or consumed.
linq.enumerablesIntro: Choose the query entry point that matches your data, all within the same library.
linq.objectDescription: Create sequences from arrays, collections or varargs, then filter, order, group and join objects.
linq.intDescription: Use Linq.ofInts for int-specific queries and numeric aggregation such as sum and average.
linq.longDescription: Use Linq.ofLongs for long-valued data, reducing unnecessary boxing and unboxing in primitive pipelines.
linq.doubleDescription: Use Linq.ofDoubles for filtering, transforming and aggregating double-valued data.
linq.features.filterDescription: Filter with where, transform with select, and slice sequences with skip and take.
linq.features.orderDescription: Combine orderBy and thenBy for multi-level sorting, or organize elements by key with groupBy.
linq.features.joinDescription: Correlate sequences with join and groupJoin; use distinct, union, intersect and except for set operations.
linq.features.aggregateDescription: Consume results with operators such as count, first and aggregate, or materialize them as lists, arrays and maps.
linq.prepareDescription: The repository README and compiler configuration require JDK 25 or later.
linq.installDescription: Choose your build tool and copy the example. Version 1.0.0 comes from the repository pom.xml; confirm publication or follow the README to build and install locally first.
linq.sampleDescription: Filter even numbers, square them, then consume the query with toArray.
linq.relatedDescription: Explore the Commons Lib utility dependency or the separate linq-in-java repository.

examples.heading: Code examples
examples.runHint: Expand an example for its complete Java class and output. Add the dependency, save the code with the displayed filename, and run main. Code and type names stay unchanged when switching languages. Examples do not change with the selected dependency version.
examples.source: View this example in the README
examples.commons.intro: Five examples adapted from Quick Examples in the Commons Lib README, with main and output statements added. Compiled and checked with Commons Lib 1.1.6.
examples.commons.namingDescription: Use StringUtils to convert between snake_case, UpperCamel and lowerCamel naming styles.
examples.commons.intervalDescription: Create a closed-open [1, 10) interval with IntInterval and check its boundaries and formatted representation.
examples.commons.counterDescription: Create a counter with Counter.atomic, increment and add to it, then read its current value.
examples.commons.functionDescription: Calculate volume with TriFunction, using full invocation, partial application and memorized result caching.
examples.commons.pairDescription: Transform the left-hand string with mappedLeft while preserving the right-hand Integer value.
examples.linq.intro: Six queries adapted from the LINQ for Java README, with imports, main and required record definitions added. Compiled and run against repository version 1.0.0 with JDK 25; see the dependency section for publication status.
examples.linq.filterDescription: Create an Int sequence with Linq.ofInts, keep even numbers with where, and obtain the result with toArray.
examples.linq.projectionDescription: Use select and String::length to turn names into lengths, then collect them into a List.
examples.linq.orderingDescription: Order by age, then by name. Person.toString preserves the README output format; the optional annotation is omitted.
examples.linq.aggregationDescription: Calculate sum and average using IntEnumerable. The README print label age is corrected to avg.
examples.linq.setsDescription: Use distinct, except, intersect and union for unique values, difference, intersection and union.
examples.linq.studentsDescription: Follow the README Student example: keep scores of at least 80, order by descending score, then select the names.
